title: Defining Physiological Subtypes in Essential Tremor
text:
Essential tremor (ET) is a prevalent neurological disorder with hetrogeneous treatment responses across
patients, potentially stemming from distinct underlying cerebellar physiological differences that require to be
investigated in order to advance precise therapeutics. Building on preliminary cerebellar
electroencephalographic (EEG) data that identified four distinct physiological ET subtypes, this K99/R00
project aims to address knowledge gaps, by defining the prevalence, tremor and clinical features of these
subtypes, uncover their cerebello-cortical network dynamics, and refine subtype classification using machine
learning. This study will provide the basis to stratify ET patients based on their cerebellar physiological
abnormalities and pave the way for the development of tailored, precise therapeutic strategies.

title: Impact of Disparities in Food Security on Glycemic Control and Health CareUtilization Among Youth and Young Adults with Diabetes
text: Good glycemic control is important for optimal health and prevention of acute and chronic complications  among people living with diabetes, but food insecurity is a serious barrier to achieving good glycemic  control, particularly among some population groups. This is the first longitudinal study that will characterize how food insecurity affects glycemic control measured by continuous glucose monitoring and the impact it has on health care utilization on a day-to-day basis in youth and young adults with type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

title: Molecular Basis of Allergic and Immunologic Disease
text:
Allergies and immune system diseases are becoming increasingly common, especially in children. Treatment
options are limited so research to identify both the roots of these disorders and possible treatments is critical.
This Training Program seeks to recruit talented young MD pediatricians and PhD scientists committed to
translational research and to prepare them for careers as productive investigators in the area of pediatric
immunology.

title: Fractionated photoimmunotherapy to harness low-dose immunostimulation in ovarian cancer
text:
Ovarian cancers have co-evolved with the patient’s immune system and build a complex tumor-immune
microenvironment. As anti-PD1 immunotherapy has generally shown poor efficacy against ovarian cancers,
there is a dire clinical need to complement checkpoint inhibition with treatments that stimulate infiltration or
proliferation of tumor-specific TC’s. We propose an integrated experimental–mathematical oncology approach
to decipher how to best harness immune sparing and immune stimulation of fractionated photoimmunotherapy
to personalize treatments for advanced or recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer patients with presently dismal
survival rates.

title: Direct capture of transcription factors bound to genomic DNA for sequence mapping and protein identification
text:
The proposed studies aim to develop methods that can accurately determine the binding sites and DNA co-binding
partners of two most dysregulated transcription factors (TFs) across all human cancers, c-Myc and p53. These studies
will not only reveal insights into the basic mechanisms of cancer initiation and progression but also develop innovative
molecular analysis tools for the study of TFs in broad biological and disease contexts.

title: SEMIColon: Somatic Exploration of Mosaicism in Colon
text:
Diseases of the colon are widespread, with colorectal cancer the 2nd leading cause of cancer death in the US
and inflammatory bowel disease highly prevalent and rising in incidence across the globe. These pathologies
have distinct presentations and outcomes across the length of the colon, but the genetic etiologies of these
differences are poorly understood and limit precision treatment. By understanding how somatic mosaicism
differs throughout the colon and disease development, we will be better equipped to treat these pathologies,
better prepared to identify at-risk individuals, and better able to study tissue-specific disease progression in
other organ systems.

title: PROJECT 1:  Genomic Vulnerabilities in Leiomyosarcoma (LMS)
text:
Project 1: Narrative 
Project 1 seeks to develop therapies that maximize intrinsic LMS genotoxic stress by targeting the key DNA 
damage response enzyme, DNA protein kinase. We have shown that most LMS have chromosomal instability 
(CIN) which creates hyper-dependence on this enzyme. The initial clinical trial in this Project tests the hypothesis 
that a very low dose of doxorubicin sensitizes LMS cells to DNA-PKi and PARPi, thereby converting CIN into a 
liability while minimizing nonneoplastic cell toxicity.

title: Therapeutic genetics and disease modeling in LAMA2-CMD
text:
LAMA2-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy (LAMA2-CMD) is a genetic disease that causes skeletal muscle
and nerve damages in children. We will evaluate the therapeutic benefits of LAMA1 upregulation to compensate
for the lack of LAMA2 in mouse and patient-derived cellular models. These findings will pave the way towards
the development of a mutation-independent therapeutic interventions for LAMA2-CMD and other muscular
dystrophies.

title: Small Molecule Therapeutic Discovery for Angelman Syndrome
text:
No effective treatment exists for Angelman syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by maternal
allele deletions of the UBE3A gene. However, activation of the epigenetically-silenced paternal UBE3A allele in
neurons offers an attractive therapeutic target. We have discovered a small molecule that can be administered
peripherally to unsilence the dormant paternal UBE3A allele throughout the brain, and we propose to advance
this small molecule towards a potentially transformative treatment for Angelman syndrome.

title: Integration of real world evidence, cell line assays, and single cell omics via deep reinforcement learning for Alzheimer's disease drug discovery
text:
Alzheimer’s disease is a currently incurable dementia, in which certain cell type and subtypes may function and
interact abnormally, leading to neuron loss and cognitive impairment. We propose deep reinforcement transfer
learning approach with feedback loops to improve identification of novel druggable cell subpopulations and
repurposable drugs. Our novel translational methodology utilizes single cell omics, real world data, and
experimental validation of repurposable drugs, using induced pluripotent stem cell lines chosen to match high
risk subpopulations of cells identified from our computational approaches, to iteratively improve our therapeutic
options for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.

title: Epstein-Barr virus nuclear antigen 2 in transcription regulation
text:
EBV infection contributes to a spectrum of diseases, including infectious mononucleosis
nasopharyngeal carcinoma, oral hairy leukoplakia, Post-Transplantation Lymphoproliferative
Disorder (PTLD), AIDS lymphomas, and certain B cell malignancies, etc. Central to EBV
oncogenesis is EBNA2, a pivotal EBV-encoded transcription factor. This study seeks to unravel
the intricate functions of EBNA2 in transcriptional regulation, with the potential to unveil novel
targets for intervening in EBV-associated diseases.

title: Statistical Innovation to Integrate Sequences and Phenotypes for Scalable Phylodynamic Inference
text:
Combating rapidly evolving pathogens, such as Dengue, Ebola, hepatitis B, HIV, inﬂuenza, mpox, SARS-CoV-2,
and yellow fever viruses, and their associated disease burden is a tremendous challenge requiring sustained
research effort and deliberate public health measures. Viral genome sequencing and phenotyping from infected
individuals as an outbreak unfolds has the potential to guide intervention and clinical management, if the phylo-
geographic and phylodynamic toolset can capture biological complexity and scale to 10,000s of samples. This
proposal aims to develop versatile and scalable statistical models and computational tools to provide this data
integration and address key questions about emerging epidemics and historical viral spread.

title: Mechanistic analysis of a combined liposome-TLR7/8-agonist adjuvanted virus-like particle vaccine
text:
This project will examine the efficacy and mechanism of action of a virus-like particle (VLP) based vaccine using
a TLR7/8 agonist paired with a second, lipid-based adjuvant. Three distinct lipid based platforms will be tested
in these combinations. We will characterize the resulting adaptive immune response and define transcriptional
signatures induced in the lymph nodes following vaccination in both murine and non-human primate models.

title: Regulation of Nutrient Homeostasis by COMMD proteins
text:
Nutrient handling is dependent on transport mechanisms across the plasma membrane of the cell, which is
required for movement across the intestine and other organs. This process is carried out by membrane proteins
that are constantly moving between the cell surface and other intracellular locations, such as the endolysosomal
network. The studies proposed here seek to uncover the molecular mode of action of newly discovered cellular
proteins that regulate the movement of nutrient transporters between the plasma membrane and the endosome,
with a specific focus on copper handling, and the impact of these processes on nutrition in living animals.

title: Core D: Long-Term Follow-Up
text:
The Long-Term Follow-Up Unit (LTFU, Core D) supports the Program by providing extended data collection and
biospecimen acquisition services to the Projects. Through a combination of chart review, annual surveys and
active contact with participants and providers, Core D is responsible for ensuring that protocol requirements
beyond the acute treatment phase (generally 2-3 months) are performed and research samples are collected.
Core D also interacts closely with Core B, which is responsible for early data collection and all data analysis.

title: Predicting response to immunotherapy with hyperpolarized 13C MRI
text:
Immunotherapy is used to treat many types of cancer, but individual responses vary, and current methods to
detect response early and accurately are insufficient. Hyperpolarized (HP) 13C magnetic resonance imaging
(MRI) is an emerging technology that may overcome these deficiencies. This project will use syngeneic models
of bladder cancer that are sensitive and resistant to immunotherapy to test the hypothesis that measurement of
glycolysis, perfusion and/or cell death by HP 13C MRI will provide a better measure of immunotherapeutic
efficacy than current standard of care imaging modalities.

title: Using Deep Multimodal Clustering to Characterize Motor Phenotypes Across the Lifespan
text:
Upper limb motor impairments are prevalent in neurologic conditions across the lifespan; however, we lack
clinically feasible assessment methods that can identify underlying impairments and target interventions to a
patient’s specific presentation. The proposed project will develop a methodology of using clinically feasible
multimodal data to cluster a large sample of neurologically intact individuals across the lifespan into “motor
phenotypes”. This methodology and normative dataset can later be applied to phenotype clinical populations,
which will be a key step towards precision rehabilitation and improve diagnosis and treatment.

title: Discovering the mechanisms underlying oncogenesis by ZFTA-RELA and pinpointing therapeutic targets.
text:
The overall goal of this proposal is to understand the mechanistic basis of ZFTA-RELA ependymoma, with a
specific focus on biomolecular condensates and impact on gene transcription and tumorigenesis. Our studies
will also evaluate the contribution of ZFTA-RELA interacting proteins as cell proliferative dependencies, and
therapeutic targets.

title: CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOMES RESEARCH TRAINING PROGRAM
text:
While it has been over 20 years since the Institute of Medicine called for more evidence-based, patient-
centered care, cardiovascular care is still highly variable and fails to achieve its full potential. The UMKC T32 in
Cardiovascular Outcomes Research trains diverse, talented post-doctoral scholars committed to improving the
quality and value of healthcare though knowledge generation, implementation and evaluation of healthcare
innovations.

title: Understanding and exploiting muscle and liver contributions to RNA-Nanoparticle immunity
text:
The objective of this study is to gain mechanistic insight into how RNA-LNP expression in muscle and liver
influences immunity, with the goal of establishing RNA designs that can boost immunity or tolerance to mRNA
payloads.
